claim: FW-0206 grain production fell 12-44 percent depending on location
reading: The book was not opened. The 12-44 percent range is not adopted.

claim: A Winchester yield comparison, not the 12-44 percent sentence
source_title: Schuh, Narratives of Environmental Events (2020), citing Titow
baseline: Titow average, as reported by Schuh
reading: Schuh says Titow calculated yields 36 percent below average for 1314/15 and 45 percent below average for 1315/16. Titow's pages were not opened.

claim: FW-0353 potato production fell roughly 86 percent in 1847
source_title: Central Statistics Office, Farming Since the Famine, Potatoes
reading: The page prints 656,014 ha in 1846 and 89,000 ha in 1847, and a pre-famine balance sheet of 15 million tons. It does not say production fell 86 percent.

claim: FW-0353 cites Bourke (1960) for the production decline
source_title: Bourke, The extent of the potato crop in Ireland at the time of the Famine (1960)
reading: The paper was not retrieved. The production percent is not adopted.

claim: FW-0367 63-94 percent of crops lost in the Madras Presidency in 1877
baseline: not stated as a loss percent
reading: Saved shares as printed: Bellary 6, Kurnool 6, Cuddapah 18, Chingleput 18, Nellore 25, North Arcot 25, Coimbatore 25, Madura 25, Salem 33, Tinnevelly 37. Davis does not print 63-94 percent lost. The Famine Commission page was not opened. Tanjore is not in the table.

claim: FW-0367 Algeria grain harvest fell 50 percent
reading: Davis writes that half of the grain harvest was lost. A separate sentence says wheat and barley exports fell by half. Footnote 53 was not opened.

claim: FW-0415 1934 US wheat fell 36 percent versus 1921-1930
source_title: NASS, Crop Production Historical Track Records, April 2023, all wheat
reading: Production, thousand bushels: 1921 818964; 1922 846649; 1923 759482; 1924 841617; 1925 668700; 1926 832213; 1927 875059; 1928 914373; 1929 824183; 1930 886522; 1934 526052. Decline against the ten-year mean is 36.37 percent. Henson (2012) and USDA (2015) were not opened. Not the Great Plains.

claim: FW-0415 1934 US corn fell 48 percent versus 1921-1930
source_title: NASS, Crop Production Historical Track Records, April 2023, corn harvested for grain

claim: FW-0463 wheat yields fell 18-22 percent from July 2002 to June 2009
source_title: van Dijk and coauthors, Water Resources Research (2013)
reading: The page says yields were 18-22 percent lower than under average conditions, and that production volume increased because a 12 percent yield decline against pre-drought years was offset by 22 percent more area. BOM (2015) was not opened.

claim: FW-0459 cites Goodkind and West (2001) for 30 percent of grain crops lost
source_title: Goodkind and West, Population and Development Review (2001)
reading: The article was not opened. The indexed abstract is a mortality range. The 30 percent crop sentence is not adopted.

claim: Government announcement of grain lost in the 1995 floods
source_title: Noland, Robinson, and Wang, Famine in North Korea (1999)
reading: The government announced 330,000 hectares destroyed and 1.9 million tons of grain lost. Outside organizations formulated far lower estimates of the damage.

claim: 1.9 million tons as about 30 percent of grain needed to feed the population
source_title: Lee, The North Korean Famine and Food Shortage (2006)
baseline: grain necessary to feed the population
reading: Lee calls 1.9 million tons about 30 percent of the grain necessary to feed the population, citing Goodkind and West page 221. That is not 30 percent of grain crops lost.

claim: FW-0341 parts of New England lost almost 100 percent of the maize crop
reading: The book was not opened. The almost-100-percent sentence is not adopted.

claim: Jefferson's expectation for the 1816 corn crop
source_title: Jefferson to Gallatin, 8 September 1816, quoted by Monticello
baseline: an ordinary crop, in his words
reading: He writes that the corn crop through the Atlantic states will probably be less than one-third of an ordinary one. It is an expectation, not a measured New England total.

source_title: Vanuatu Post-Disaster Needs Assessment, Cyclone Pam
reading: Crop damage VT 131596 thousand plus crop losses VT 4043278 thousand. Total crop effects VT 4174874 thousand, summarized as VT 4175 million. Kava is 58 percent of crop losses. Not cereal tonnes.

source_title: FAO, 2025 CFSAM to the Republic of the Sudan, March 2026
baseline: previous year and previous five-year average
reading: About 5.2 million tonnes, 22 percent below the previous year and 19 percent below the five-year average. National production. The mission cites inputs, with rainfall offsetting part of the conflict constraint.
